question_record.context: During the investigation of a suspicious access to the LSASS service, which might indicate an attempt to decrypt user passwords, several suspicious files (`hid.dll`, `winscard.dll`, `cryptdll.dll`, `vaultcli.dll`) were observed being utilized. In addition, a PowerShell command was observed being executed remotely with the following command line: `powershell.exe -noexit -command set-location -literalpath 'c:\users\bjenkins\downloads\midnight14'`. Suspicious remote activities were noted on the machine associated with multiple system and network alterations.
question_record.question: During the investigation, it was determined that an account accessed the DKM key of an ADFS object. What is the email address of the account that performed this action?
solution: There was a suspicious access to the LSASS service using the process `lsass.exe`.
Suspicious remote activity was detected involving an account with SID `S-2-5-21-571436798-3864380397-1837441745-3206`.
An account with the email `gsmith@niseko.alpineskihouse.co` read the DKM key of ADFS object with ID `4cac49d3-29d3-407e-8c9b-b7ebb21541b2`.

45.name: Suspicious access to LSASS service
45.description: In order to obtain clear-text password, attackers must decrypt the user's password from the LSASS service's memory. Multiple public tools as well as custom ones could be used to perform this operation. Once obtained, these credentials are often used in lateral movement activities to infiltrate other machines and servers in the network.

37.name: Suspicious remote activity
37.description: Suspicious activity initiated remotely was observed on this machine. This alert can flag attempts to initiate interactive sessions, modify files, pass WMI commands, create scheduled tasks, and other potentially malicious activities from a remote machine.

106.name: Suspected AD FS DKM key read
106.description: gsmith read the DKM key of ADFS object id 4cac49d3-29d3-407e-8c9b-b7ebb21541b2
